title: a-seal-snapshots-cairn-once-per-batch-and-binds-what-it-only-reads
intention: Sealing a proof no longer copies all of ~/.cairn per proof: logs get an empty writable scratch, the aider shim's data binds read-only, ~/.cairn is snapshotted once per batch, and each proof's private copy comes from that pristine snapshot.
why: Every seal copies ~425MB of ~/.cairn twice (measured 2026-09-06): 208MB of it is logs, 91MB the aider shim's data, neither of which a proof needs a private writable copy of. Today's 18 re-seals moved ~15GB to prove code that had not changed. The lived symptom is a seal that takes tens of seconds when the proof takes one.
how: In the tester's bubblewrap setup: `--ro-bind` the aider shim's data dir; mount a fresh tmpfs (or empty dir) at the sandbox's ~/.cairn/logs so a proof that logs still can, into something discarded; take one snapshot of the rest of ~/.cairn per `--seal` batch under the tester's scratch root and `cp -a --reflink=auto` per proof from it (reflink is free on btrfs/xfs, a plain copy elsewhere). bubblewrap 0.9.0 here has no overlay; a true copy-on-write swap waits on 0.10+ and is out of this ticket.
falsifier: DONE when: (1) bytes copied per proof, measured by du of the per-proof scratch before teardown, drop from ~850MB to under 150MB; (2) a batch of N proofs copies ~/.cairn once (one snapshot dir, N reflinks/copies); (3) a proof that writes ~/.cairn/logs still passes and the real logs are byte-identical after; (4) every currently-green seal re-seals green under the new sandbox (no proof depended on a writable aider dir — if one does, it is named and the bind for that dir becomes rw for that proof only). WRONG INTENT if a proof legitimately reads recent logs and the empty scratch breaks it — then logs bind ro and the proof's log writes go to a shadow path.
traces_to: Law 1 — copying logs nobody reads is the resolver (and the disk) spent on the settled. CP4 — designing to the tool: the sandbox exists so a proof cannot touch the real instance, and that is satisfied by binding what is only read.
